en.question: Which two statements about defending an agentic application are correct? (Select 2)

options.text: Guardrails should be layered, because no single control is sufficient alone.
Capability restriction beats instruction: an unreachable action cannot be induced.
A sufficiently detailed system prompt removes the need for authorisation checks.
options.note: Prompts never replace authorisation; they are guidance rather than enforcement.

options.text: Prompt injection is fully solved by sanitising input before it reaches the model.
options.note: Sanitisation helps, but adversaries rephrase, encode, and translate around it.

options.text: Running every request at temperature 0 prevents jailbreak attempts succeeding.
options.note: Temperature has no bearing on susceptibility to adversarial instructions.

en.explanation: Defence in depth is the governing principle, and the strongest single layer is capability restriction, because an action the agent structurally cannot take cannot be triggered by any input.
